The '''National Vital Statistics System''' ('''NVSS''') is an inter-governmental system of sharing data on the [[vital statistics (government records)|vital statistics]] of the [[population of the United States]]. It involves coordination between the different state health departments of the US states and the [[National Center for Health Statistics]], a division of the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]].<ref name=about>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/about_nvss.htm|title = About the National Vital Statistics System|accessdate = April 22, 2014|publisher = National Vital Statistics System}}</ref>

==Data and publications==

The National Vital Statistics System includes the following data sets and publications:<ref name=about/>

* Vital Statistics of the United States:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/vsus.htm|title = Vital Statistics of the United States|publisher = [[National Center for Health Statistics]]|accessdate = April 22, 2014}}</ref> The data set goes back to 1890.
* National Vital Statistics Report:<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/nvsr.htm|title = National Vital Statistics Reports|publisher = [[National Center for Health Statistics]]|accessdate = April 22, 2014}}</ref> This is a monthly report that goes back to January 1998. The earlier version of this report, called the Monthly Vital Statistics Report, goes back to July 1964.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/mvsr.htm|title = Monthly Vital Statistics Reports|publisher = [[National Center for Health Statistics]]|accessdate = April 22, 2014}}</ref>
* Other reports<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products.htm|title = Products|publisher = [[National Center for Health Statistics]]|accessdate = April 22, 2014}}</ref>

All data is accessible online on the NVSS website.

==Related programs==

The following programs are related to the National Vital Statistics System:<ref name=about/>

* Linked Birth and Infant Death Data Set
* [[National Survey of Family Growth]]
* Matched Multiple Birth Data Set
* National Death Index
* National Maternal and Infant Health Survey
* National Mortality Followback Survey

==Reception and impact==

===Academic research===

Data from the National Vital Statistics System has been cited in academic research on many topics, including births<ref>{{cite journal|title = Are preterm births on the decline in the United States? Recent data from the National Vital Statistics System.|pmid = 20604990|journal = NCHS Data Brief|volume = 39|year = 2010|pages = 1–8|last1 = Martin|first1 = J. A.|last2 = Osterman|first2 = M. J.|last3 = Sutton|first3 = P. D.|issue = 39}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title = Recent Trends in Cesarean Delivery in the United States|journal = NCHS Data Brief|volume = 35|date = March 2010|accessdate = April 22, 2014|url = http://www.gapha.org/wp-content/uploads/2010/03/cesarean.pdf}}</ref> and homicides.<ref>{{cite journal|title = A Comparison of Supplementary Homicide Reports and National Vital Statistics System Homicide Estimates for U.S. Counties|doi = 10.1177/1088767900004004002|last1 = Wiersema|first1 = Brian|last2 = Loftin|first2 = Colin|last3 = McDowall|first3 = David|journal = [[Homicide Studies]]|volume = 4|issue = 4|pages = 317–340|date = November 2000}}</ref>

A 1995 paper by Weed for [[Population Index]] described the history of NVSS and how to prepare it for the next century.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://popindex.princeton.edu/Articles/Weed.html|title = Vital Statistics in the United States: Preparing for the Next Century|last = Weed|first = James A.|journal = [[Population Index]]|publisher = [[Office of Population Research]], [[Princeton University]]|volume = 61|issue = 4|pages = 527–539|date = Winter 1995|accessdate = April 22, 2014|doi = 10.2307/3645558|jstor = 3645558| pmid=12347152 |url-access = subscription}}</ref>

===Use as a standard source===

Libraries and other link collections have pointed to the NVSS as an [[official statistics|official data]] source for the [[vital statistics (government records)|vital statistics]] of the [[United States]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.libraries.iub.edu/index.php?pageId=400&resourceId=2273819|title = National Vital Statistics System|publisher = [[Indiana University Bloomington]]|accessdate = April 22, 2014}}</ref>
